lines.trans: Hello, Vitya, what do you think, will my wife forgive me?
That depends on how hard you try.
I will try hard, because an actor's career is very short.
Today you are a star, and tomorrow they will kick you off television.
And here there are four floors and an excellent restaurant.
Tell me, is she in her office right now?
No, she just recently came out to have dinner.

examples.text: Приятного аппетита!
examples.trans: Enjoy your meal!

examples.text: У него хороший аппетит.
examples.trans: He has a good appetite.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Для меня это будет отличный подарок!
examples.trans: For me that will be an excellent gift!

examples.text: Катя, привет, эти красивые цветы для тебя.
examples.trans: Katya, hi, these beautiful flowers are for you.

examples.text: Иначе для всех это будет просто небезопасно.
examples.trans: Otherwise it will simply be unsafe for everyone.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'юрприз'). Common masculine noun meaning 'surprise' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Элечка, приятного аппетита, у меня для тебя сюрприз.
examples.trans: Elechka, enjoy your meal, I have a surprise for you.

examples.text: Я вам сюрприз покажу один.
examples.trans: I'll show you one surprise.

examples.text: Какой сюрприз?
examples.trans: What surprise?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Если мне не веришь, спроси у неё.
examples.trans: If you do not believe me, ask her.

examples.text: Если идёте на день рождения, дарим деньги.
examples.trans: If you are coming to my birthday, we are gifting money.

examples.text: Если ты считаешь это нормальным, ты безумец!
examples.trans: If you consider this normal, you are out of your mind!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'нова').

examples.text: Заодно вкусного кофе попьёте и снова поцелуетесь.
examples.trans: At the same time you will drink tasty coffee and kiss again.

examples.text: Я так понимаю, она снова не согласилась.
examples.trans: As I understand it, she did not agree again.

examples.text: Гуля сказала, сегодня можно снова у них переночевать.
examples.trans: Gulya said tonight I can stay overnight at their place again.

meanings.en: to see, to catch sight of
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'I will see', paired with 'видеть'.

examples.text: Вот увидишь!
examples.trans: You'll see!

examples.text: Я увидел папу.
examples.trans: I saw Dad.

examples.text: И Нину свою ты больше не увидишь!
examples.trans: And you'll never see your Nina again!

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'анитар'). Common masculine noun meaning 'orderlies' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Если снова увижу санитаров, ударю тебя бутылкой!
examples.trans: If I see orderlies again, I will hit you with a bottle!

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть санитар.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always orderlies.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to punch
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'дарить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will hit', paired with 'ударять'.

examples.text: Ну, давай, ударь меня!
examples.trans: Well, come on, hit me!

examples.text: Он ударил кулаком по столу.
examples.trans: He struck the table with his fist.

examples.text: Вот если бы он ребёнка ударил!
examples.trans: Now if he had hit a child!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'bottle' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Привет, кроме шеф-повара некому бутылку принести?
examples.trans: Hello, is there nobody besides the head chef to bring a bottle?

examples.text: Если снова увижу санитаров, ударю тебя бутылкой!
examples.trans: If I see orderlies again, I will hit you with a bottle!

examples.text: С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: With a bottle of wine in your hand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'invited', paired with 'звать'.

examples.text: Нет, я Диму позвал, он мириться приехал.
examples.trans: No, I called Dima, he came to make peace.

examples.text: Какого ещё Диму ты сюда ко мне позвал?
examples.trans: What Dima did you call here to see me?

examples.text: Даже Нагиева специально ради меня сюда позвал.
examples.trans: You even specially called Nagiyev here for my sake.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Виктор, она уволила семь горничных за три дня.
examples.trans: Viktor, she fired seven maids in three days.

examples.text: Ничего, она немного поплачет и скоро успокоится.
examples.trans: It is fine, she will cry a little and calm down soon.

examples.text: Иначе она сегодня весь отель разнесёт!
examples.trans: Otherwise she will tear the whole hotel apart today!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to make peace', paired with 'помириться'.

examples.text: Нет, я Диму позвал, он мириться приехал.
examples.trans: No, I called Dima, he came to make peace.

examples.text: Значит, помирить нас сегодня решил?
examples.trans: So you decided to reconcile us today?

examples.text: Беги скорее с Ваней мириться!
examples.trans: Run quickly to make peace with Vanya!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'came', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.text: Нет, я Диму позвал, он мириться приехал.
examples.trans: No, I called Dima, he came to make peace.

examples.text: Ты на какой машине приехала?
examples.trans: Which car did you come in?

examples.text: Паша приехал.
examples.trans: Pasha has arrived.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'what (of what)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Как замечательно ты придумал жить всем вместе.
examples.trans: How wonderfully you thought of living all together.

examples.text: А тебе вообще какая до этого разница?
examples.trans: And what difference does that even make to you?

examples.text: Ладно, вам как девушкам можно меньше сдать.
examples.trans: Alright, as girls you can chip in a bit less.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Потом ещё спасибо скажешь на нашей рыбалке.
examples.trans: Later you will thank me on our fishing trip.

examples.text: Честно говоря, мы пока ещё точно не знаем.
examples.trans: Honestly speaking, we do not know for sure yet.

examples.text: Денег мне хватает или ещё у официантов просить.
examples.trans: Whether I have enough money or need to ask the waiters too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Быстро вызывай сюда врача!
examples.trans: Quickly call the doctor here!

examples.text: Я серьёзно, нужно срочно привезти сюда Нагиева.
examples.trans: I am serious, we need to urgently bring Nagiyev here.

examples.text: Какого ещё Диму ты сюда ко мне позвал?
examples.trans: What Dima did you call here to see me?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'to', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Скажи, чего ты так радостно улыбаешься?
examples.trans: Tell me, why are you smiling so cheerfully?

examples.text: Виктор, она уволила семь горничных за три дня.
examples.trans: Viktor, she fired seven maids in three days.

examples.text: Миша, мне сегодня некогда с ней сидеть.
examples.trans: Misha, I have no time to babysit her today.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Лёва, вставай, мне твою кровать перестирать надо.
examples.trans: Lyova, get up, I need to rewash your bed.

examples.text: Во-первых, это совершенно не твоё личное дело.
examples.trans: First of all, it is none of your personal business at all.

examples.text: Я тебе твой любимый луковый суп приготовил.
examples.trans: I cooked your favorite onion soup for you.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'husband' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Никогда в жизни не верь хитрым мужчинам!
examples.trans: Never in your life trust sly men!

examples.text: Попробуйте спокойно понять и простить своего мужа.
examples.trans: Try to calmly understand and forgive your husband.

examples.text: Самое главное — исключить бывшего мужа из жизни.
examples.trans: The most important thing is to exclude the ex-husband from her life.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here, there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот и иди дальше к своей подруге.
examples.trans: Then keep going to your friend.

examples.text: Вот говорила мне мама идти учиться в музыканты!
examples.trans: My mom used to tell me to go study to be a musician!

examples.text: Твоего мужа Нагиева, вот он идёт к нам!
examples.trans: Your husband Nagiyev, here he comes toward us!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is coming', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Вот говорила мне мама идти учиться в музыканты!
examples.trans: My mom used to tell me to go study to be a musician!

examples.text: Я иду домой.
examples.trans: I'm going home.

examples.text: Он идёт на второй срок.
examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы собирались кофе попить, а ты молчишь.
examples.trans: We were going to drink coffee, and you are silent.

examples.text: А во-вторых, да, мы с ним встречаемся.
examples.trans: And second of all, yes, he and I are dating.

examples.text: Да, мы с ним встречаемся!
examples.trans: Yes, he and I are dating!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Катя, постой, ведь это ничего не значит.
examples.trans: Katya, wait, after all that means nothing.

examples.text: Раз я спрашиваю, значит, мне есть разница.
examples.trans: Since I am asking, that means it makes a difference to me.

examples.text: Значит, помирить нас сегодня решил?
examples.trans: So you decided to reconcile us today?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мирить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'reconcile'.

examples.text: Значит, помирить нас сегодня решил?
examples.trans: So you decided to reconcile us today?

examples.text: Понятно, что их надо быстро помирить.
examples.trans: Clearly, one must reconcile them quickly.

examples.text: Когда-нибудь ты захочешь помириться со своим папой.
examples.trans: Someday you'll want to make peace with your dad.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.text: Значит, помирить нас сегодня решил?
examples.trans: So you decided to reconcile us today?

examples.text: Суд решил.
examples.trans: The court has decided.

examples.text: Я решил.
examples.trans: I've decided.
